status: Reproduced soil-rendering defect corrected and verified; exact recorded save/location not identified.

recording.gnomeOverview: User confirmed intentional desktop input. No input implementation change. Blur, focusout and hidden-document reset checks pass.

path: WorldGenerator -> placeMud: legitimate saved mud cells beside the river
PixiRenderer.buildChunk -> neighbourMaterialMask: final whole-world neighbor data
createWaterTextures: tile-local edgeDistance and fixed corner clipping, repeated local hash, 0.70/0.94 alpha
rootCause.failure: A near-opaque soil interior with only a narrow tile-local fringe and three opacity levels was stamped independently into each 32x32 mud cell. Rectangular groups follow saved mud occupancy; blending stops at adjacent grass cells. This is reproducible in original production WebGL, not a missing texture or a shadow/collision rectangle.
rootCause.otherSystems: Inspected river carving and smoothing, hills/elevation, bank masks, source frame selection, chunk caching and layer order. No generation or collision change was justified by the reproduced defect. Raised cliff art and movement use the shared final-cell elevation topology; mud is traversable slow ground.

evidence.originalPureRaster: original-raster.txt is an extraction of the original mask/hash/alpha formula. baseline-regression.txt records two failing regression assertions before correction.
evidence.originalProduction: scripts/capture-original-soil.mjs builds the original terrainArt/waterArt from 58baaf85064efd55fce239e3f0e05ec35276c940 and reverses only the soil integration in the current renderer, preserving pre-existing portal changes. Build output is /tmp/forest-mud-original-dist; originals and the working tree are not overwritten.
evidence.browserRedGreen: Identical WebGL regression fails in Chromium and Firefox on original renderer (sample difference about 21/255) and passes on corrected renderer within 4/255 rounding tolerance. original-browser-regression.txt retains failures.
evidence.comparison: comparison.png: original left, corrected right; rows are seeds 1, 42, 123, 1337. Native-size captures are in before/ and after/. Default-effect captures and collider/chunk-boundary captures were visually inspected.

solution: Reconstruct continuous cell-centred soil coverage from saved terrain, normalize land weights at water boundaries, and sample pigment/fringe grain in world coordinates.
Rasterize affected low-ground cells into sparse chunk atlases, composed after grass and before flowers/contact shadows. Remove old soil_patch textures.
Release atlas frames and sources on chunk replacement, world replacement and renderer teardown.
No terrain regeneration, collision changes, seed exceptions, coordinate offsets, save migrations, or covering effects. Existing soil palette, water/cliff art and default atmospheric effects remain.

unitIntegration.coverage: All 256 neighbor material arrangements, bank transitions, water/raised-surface exclusions, deterministic/read-only rasterization, chunk atlas packing/edit rebuild/destruction; inherited generation, collision and save coverage.

resize.note: Same two browser pixel regressions rechecked at three viewport sizes, including integer zoom change; not additional unique test cases.

verification.existingSaves: All four static pre-repair v10 world fixtures loaded in both browsers. Whole saved-world equality passed after load; new saves also survived camera visibility cycling and reload. Inherited legacy-save unit and browser cases pass.

checks.lint: 0 errors; 5 pre-existing landscape non-null assertion warnings

verification.intermediateFailures: An overlapping browser invocation lost its shared preview server; independent preview and sequential rerun passed. One full unit run concurrent with browsers exceeded the existing 5-second generation-test timeout. Retained in unit-contended-run.txt; isolated final full run passed without changing tests/timeouts or generation.

remainingIssues: The recording does not expose seed or numerical coordinates. Its exact save/location was not available; no claim of exact-location verification.
Visual coverage is representative, not every seed/camera position. Terrain itself remains a grid; legitimate water and cliff silhouettes are preserved.
workspace: All pre-existing uncommitted work retained. No commit, push or deployment.
